data.title: SAP Reportedly Weighs Cutting 10,000 Jobs as It Shifts Toward AI
data.description:
German business software giant SAP (SAP) is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs, or roughly 9% of its global workforce of more than 113,000 employees. The potential cuts are part of CEO Christian Klein's plan to focus more of the company's business on artificial intelligence. According to Bloomberg, the plan is still being discussed, and the final number of job cuts could change after negotiations with employee representatives. SAP has not confirmed any layoffs.

The possible cuts come as SAP changes how it develops and sells its products. The company makes software that businesses use for everyday tasks such as managing payroll and tracking inventory. SAP now wants to add more AI features to those programs so that customers can complete certain tasks with less manual work.

For example, its Joule AI assistant helps businesses complete tasks by using information from their own systems. However, developing and selling these tools requires different skills, which could change where SAP needs employees and how it spends money.

As a result, managers throughout the company have been asked to identify potential job cuts. The product development and sales departments are expected to receive particular attention. SAP had already taken steps in this direction in July, when it limited new hiring mainly to important AI positions and restricted business travel unrelated to AI work.

SAP's Previous Restructuring Cost €3.2 Billion

This would not be SAP's first major round of job cuts. In 2024, the company began a restructuring that affected around 10,000 positions and cost approximately €3.2 billion, largely because of severance payments and other employee-related expenses. Many employees left voluntarily, while others received training to move into different roles.

Interestingly, SAP's overall workforce continued to grow. It had 110,730 full-time-equivalent employees in September 2025, compared to 113,076 in September 2026.

Its revenue has also increased. Third-quarter sales grew by 13% to €10.27 billion, while revenue from cloud software rose by 26% to €6.67 billion. SAP also reported €24.1 billion in cloud revenue under contract that it expects to earn over the next 12 months, up by 28% from a year earlier.

Is SAP Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on SAP stock. This is based on seven Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average SAP price target of $270.07 per share implies 29% upside potential. (See SAP Stock Forecast).

data.title: Who Owns Okta Stock Ahead of Q3 Earnings on December 1?
data.description:
Identity and access management solutions provider Okta (OKTA) will announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings on December 1. Okta stock has rallied 133% year-to-date as the company sees solid demand amid growing adoption of agentic AI and rising cyberattacks. Heading into Q3 FY27 earnings, let's look at who owns Okta stock and what to expect from the upcoming results.

Who Owns Okta Stock?

According to TipRanks' Ownership Tool, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) own 30.44% of Okta.

They are followed by other institutional investors, mutual funds, public companies and individual investors, and insiders at 27.34%, 26.23%, 15.84%, and 0.15%, respectively.

Looking closely at the top shareholders, BlackRock (BLK) holds the largest stake in Okta at 12.40%, followed by Vanguard at 8.80%.

Among the top ETF holders, Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) holds 2.51% of Okta, while First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR) owns 2.36%. Also, Vanguard Small-Cap ETF (VB) holds 2.24%.

Moving to mutual funds, Vanguard Index Funds holds 7.98% of Okta. Meanwhile, Fidelity Select Portfolios owns 3.04%.

Wall Street's Expectations Ahead of Okta's Q3 Earnings

Wall Street expects Okta to report Q3 FY27 earnings per share (EPS) of $0.93, reflecting 13.4% year-over-year growth. Revenue is projected to rise about 10% to about $816 million.

Ahead of Q3 FY27 earnings, JPMorgan analyst Brian Essex reiterated a Buy rating on Okta stock and raised his price target to $214 from $190. The 5-star analyst expects the company to report continued momentum in the fiscal third quarter, driven by steady core demand and a growing agent security pipeline. Essex expects the company to deliver strong results, backed by expansion of business with large enterprises and partner-led deals. He also expects the company to benefit from continued new-product attach across workforce and customer identity.

"Execution is in focus after a strong 1H, and we think OKTA's stable, tenured sales force can extend that traction into 3Q," Essex said. He expects the company's demand pipeline to keep growing, as an intense threat environment accelerates identity modernization projects.

Is Okta a Good Stock to Buy Now?

data.title: Rivian vs. Lucid: Which EV Stock Is the Better Buy After Their YTD Plunge?
data.description:
Shares of U.S. electric vehicle maker Rivian (RIVN) are down roughly 50% since the start of the year to about $11.71. Its rival Lucid (LCID) is worse off, with shares down about 76% year-to-date. This comes as both EV makers are still racing to turn a net profit. On Wall Street, analysts are more bullish on Rivian, but Lucid offers the bigger upside of about 128%.

Why Rivian and Lucid Shares Have Sold Off This Year

Rivian shares have sold off this year as the automaker continues to burn cash and post losses. In the third quarter, net loss was $913 million. The EV maker used up $1.12 billion in free cash flow during the quarter.

This took the shine off its revenue, which rose 38% year-over-year to $2.2 billion. Rivian posted record quarterly deliveries of 19,248 units during the period. Demand for the R2, its new and more affordable SUV, drove revenue growth.

Likewise, Rivian shares have fallen as its EV credits have dried up due to changes in federal policy. In addition to the R2's lower prices, this development hurt the automaker's automotive gross margin in the third quarter.

Notably, Lucid shares also faced pressure amid recent bankruptcy rumors that the company promptly denied.

Why Analysts Like Rivian Better

Analysts are more bullish on Rivian than Lucid. Seaport Global analyst Ronald Jewsikow recently called RIVN stock a Buy. He sees room for the stock to gain beyond Rivian's planned vehicle lineup. 

Five-star Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois also recently upgraded Rivian shares from Hold to Buy. He pointed to demand for the R2. According to Houchois, Rivian converted more customer preorders for the high-end R2 launch trim into actual sales than it expected.

By contrast, Jewsikow started coverage of Lucid with a Sell rating. He argued that the EV maker would need significant capital to develop and launch the three new midsize vehicles it is planning.

Meanwhile, four-star Baird analyst Ben Kallo recently maintained his Hold rating on Lucid. However, Kallo noted that Lucid's efforts to reduce expenses are beginning to show results. He also pointed to the carmaker's progress in developing its self-driving technology.

Which EV Stock Is the Better Buy?

As mentioned earlier, Rivian (RIVN) has the better consensus analyst rating: a Moderate Buy. However, TipRanks' Stock Comparison tool shows that Lucid (LCID) offers the bigger upside of about 128%.

data.title: 3 Beaten-Down AI Stocks Analysts Say Could Double in Price
data.description:
AI stocks just had their worst selloff since 2020, and some are now down more than 50% in a matter of months. However, there is some silver lining. Analysts still rate all three of these names a Strong Buy. In this article we break down Cerebras Systems (CBRS), Oracle (ORCL) and Applied Digital (APLD): what each company does, what their latest earnings showed, and what Wall Street analysts are saying now.

We also made a video –

CBRS

The stock has dropped just over 71% in the last 12 months. Cerebras is the chip side of the AI trade. Instead of cutting a silicon wafer into a lot of small chips, Cerebras builds one giant chip. It sells AI computing systems built around that chip along with cloud access for training and running AI models.

It recently released Q3 earnings reporting record revenue and raising guidance. Its numbers were driven by its cloud and services business. However, it also currently expects flattish sequential cloud revenue in Q4. Management said this is not driven by pricing or demand, but entirely by limited data center capacity.

It said it took longer than expected to contract for and bring online the data center capacity required under its OpenAI agreement, leaving the company behind schedule on initial tranches. Management expects to be back on schedule in the second half of 2027.

Matt Bryson, a 5-star analyst at Wedbush raised his price target on the stock to $205 from $190 describing strong expectations for sales and profitability in Q4.

Cerebras has a Strong Buy consensus based on 9 Buy ratings. It has an average price target of $215.22, implying a 139.99% upside.

ORCL

Its stock is down 46% this year. Most people know Oracle for its data-based software which runs inside a huge share of big companies. Lately, the story has been Oracle cloud infrastructure. It is spending heavily to build AI data centers and rent their computing power to AI companies. Investors are questioning how ORCL is going to finance this.

It recently posted Q1 earnings, reporting record revenues boosted by demand for cloud infrastructure. However, gross margin declined as expected due to the ramp-up of data centers and the acceleration of infrastructure revenue.

On TipRanks, ORCL has a Strong Buy consensus with 28 Buy, 4 Hold and 1 Sell ratings. Its average price target is $241.83, implying a 132.80% upside.

APLD

Its stock is down around 50% this year. Applied Digital Corporation designs, develops, and operates digital infrastructure solutions to high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence industries in North America. It operates through: Data Center Hosting Business, and HPC Hosting Business. The company offers infrastructure services to crypto mining customers; and GPU computing solutions for critical workloads related to AI, machine learning, and other HPC tasks.

Earlier in November the company said it had signed an 18-year lease agreement with a tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler for 150 MW of IT capacity.

Under the terms of this lease deal, Applied Digital will receive $5.4 billion in base-term contracted revenue. The company said that this could increase to $12.7 billion if all renewal options are exercised over a 33-year total term. It also noted that this deal brings its total contracted base-term lease revenue to more than $41 billion, or over $100 billion if all renewal options are exercised.

On TipRanks, APLD has a Strong Buy consensus based on 7 Buy and 2 Hold ratings. It has an average price target of $41.13, implying a 234.62% upside.

data.title: U.S. Dollar Stays Near 2026 Peak in Thin Holiday Trade as 3.3% Core PCE Tops Estimates
data.description:
The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) traded near 103.72 on Thursday, pausing just below its 2026 peak near 104 in thin Thanksgiving trade. Hotter U.S. data keeps the dollar in front. October core personal consumption expenditures inflation hit 3.3% year-on-year, beating the 3.2% forecast, alongside an upward revision to third-quarter GDP.

These readings cemented bets for a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December and another in early 2027, Reuters reported. ING Global Head of Markets Chris Turner wrote Thursday that any dollar dip should stay shallow. "The problem is that the central drivers of dollar strength – a strong US economy, inflation above target and a hawkish Fed – remain fully intact," Turner said.

President Donald Trump also proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners on Wednesday, though Mizuho Bank economist Vishnu Varathan told Reuters the currency move stayed calmer than in 2025. "This is more of a defensive dollar strength than it is an aggressive loss of trade support for Asian currencies," Varathan said.

ECB Minutes Back a December Hike as Euro Holds Near $1.097

The euro (EUR/USD) held near $1.097 on Thursday, aiming for a third straight day of gains after hitting a 19-month low earlier this week. Support came from the European Central Bank's Oct. 28-29 meeting minutes, released Thursday. "A large number of members noted that, as the incoming data since the September Governing Council meeting had confirmed the case for further policy tightening, they could have supported raising interest rates at the current meeting," the account showed.

ING economist Carsten Brzeski wrote Thursday that "a December hike looks almost like a done deal," though he warned high energy costs and tighter credit could weigh on eurozone growth in 2027.

BoE Rate Bets on a Stable Pound Near $1.31

Sterling (GBP/USD) traded nearly flat near $1.3107 on Thursday, stabilizing after falling in 13 of the prior 16 sessions and losing over 2% against the dollar this month to hit November 2025 lows. The pound also slipped to 83.76 pence per euro.

Money markets still price three more Bank of England rate hikes by September 2027, Reuters noted, even after Governor Andrew Bailey said UK inflation could peak lower if energy prices stabilize. Separately, the BoE's Financial Stability Report kept the UK bank capital buffer at 2%, noting lenders stay well funded even as energy-heavy firms face tighter credit.

BoJ Hike Warnings Leave Yen Stuck Near 159

USD/JPY sat near 159.30 on Thursday as higher U.S. rate bets collided with Tokyo's threat to intervene near 160.

Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura urged faster rate hikes on Thursday to stop rising raw material costs and a weak yen from lifting inflation. Still, Forex.com analysts noted wide U.S.-Japan rate gaps keep capping yen gains, while Japanese insurers have cut currency hedging to record lows, The Japan Times reported.

data.title: Retail Stocks to Watch as the Battle for $1 Trillion in Holiday Sales Intensifies
data.description:
U.S. retailers are racing to cross $1 trillion in holiday sales for the first time this year. Notably, many see Thanksgiving Day on Thursday as the start of the U.S. holiday and shopping season. Black Friday sales start tomorrow, November 27, followed by Cyber Monday on November 30. As a result, the race to capture holiday sales has begun in earnest. Several retail stocks are worth watching, including Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT), and Costco (COST).

  • Amazon (AMZN) — Amazon is the world's largest company by sales. It generated $716.9 billion in net sales in 2025, up by 12% from $638 billion the previous year. That number is expected to rise 25% to $892.2 billion this year. Beyond its cloud business, Amazon is also an e-commerce giant. It sells goods online and offers other merchants a place to sell. According to Bernstein analyst Zhihan Ma, Amazon and Walmart are "the most obvious e-commerce destinations" among shoppers. Amazon has said it is expanding its Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals to 12 days. This is the largest such extension in the company's history.
  • Walmart (WMT) — Walmart is the world's second-largest company by sales. It was recently overtaken by Amazon. In fiscal 2026 (which ended in January 2026), its sales rose 4.7% to $713.2 billion. In October, Walmart announced early dates for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. It also recently launched a program to help members save $100 yearly. Telsey Advisory Group analysts have said that Walmart "should be another winner this holiday season."
  • Costco (COST) — Costco is a big-box retailer known for offering quality bulk purchases at the lowest prices possible. Analysts have continued to praise the retailer's ability to compete on pricing. During fiscal 2026, which ended in August, Costco's net sales reached $269.9 billion, up 10.2% from the previous year. Sales have continued to rise afterward.
  • Target (TGT) — Target is a discount and general merchandise retailer. The company's efforts to improve sales are starting to pay off. About a week ago, Target reported its third-quarter 2026 sales. It posted its strongest growth in more than five years.
  • Best Buy (BBY) — Best Buy is an electronics and appliances retailer. The company's business has been under pressure as chip shortages forced producers to raise the prices of electronic products. Still, Best Buy reported its best same-store sales in five years this week. It also raised its fiscal 2027 sales forecast.

data.title: Is It Time for Boeing (NYSE:BA) to Get Out of Space?
data.description:
I have long been concerned about aerospace stock Boeing's (BA) space ambitions. These have not gone well at all. Boeing's part of the United Launch Alliance (ULA), along with Lockheed Martin (LMT), has been marked by failed launches, delays, and enough cost overruns to make even a senator concerned. This is before Starliner, which might be regarded as the crown jewel of Boeing's space failures. At least, it might have been until Boeing and the ULA tried to launch a Vulcan rocket loaded with 40 of Amazon's (AMZN) Leo satellites for its internet constellation…and destroyed the whole thing.

So with this litany of failures behind Boeing's space ambitions, is it time for Boeing to get out of space? Or maybe, it is time for something else. One of our readers, cleinad, made an interesting suggestion: perhaps it was time for Boeing to spin off its space ambitions into a separate operation. It is an idea that could stand some examination, so as you enjoy your turkey dinner, or perhaps the anticipation of same depending on when you read this, let's have a closer look at Boeing, space, and why it may be time for Boeing to get out, and form a new spin-off, which for now, we will refer to by the hypothetical name "Boeing Space."

An Idea That is Flying High

Boeing has several space-related ambitions that could fit easily into a separate company. It has the Starliner program, of course. It has its own portion of the ULA, and the Space Launch System (SLS) operations. It has satellite manufacturing operations, and some government and commercial space operations that could be folded into a reasonable facsimile of a company. Certainly not one as big as Boeing, but one that could sustain its own stock.

This would be a move that is intensely good for Boeing. Without the space operations weighing Boeing's balance sheet down, and delivering a range of black eyes to its quality reputation—which has had enough trouble on its own of late thanks to the Alaska Airlines (ALK) incident, among others—Boeing's own fortunes might improve as it would only have the defense and commercial air operations to worry about.

Certainly, this would make corporate governance a lot easier to deal with. With Boeing Space having its own board, its own CEO, and the like, it would be able to focus much harder on building its own operations. In fact, Boeing even has most of the basics of this structure set up; Steve Parker serves as the CEO of Boeing Defense, Space, and Security. Breaking off Boeing's commercial airlines division from defense, space and security would allow Boeing to better focus on commercial air and prevent the space operations from continuing to drag on Boeing's reputation.

Not All So Positive, Though

All that being said, there are some issues for Boeing Space to address. One of the biggest is that it has a track record so laden with failures it almost looks like the space equivalent of DeLorean Motor Works. Between a space capsule that left its astronauts stranded aboard the International Space Station for most of a year—only to be brought home by a competitor's craft—and a rocket that managed to blow up its own cargo, this is not the kind of thing that fires investor confidence.

However, this might be fixable. If Boeing Space sets its IPO price low, and limits its shares to be sufficiently scarce to not be automatically worthless, Boeing Space might well pull in some investors willing to take a gamble on a long shot. Institutional investors might avoid Boeing Space like the plague on fire in a bad part of town, but retail investors might regard it as a new kind of low-yield lottery ticket. All it takes is one win to double your money, after all, and with a sufficiently low bar to entry, that could turn into something. Plus, if Boeing Space can get its act together, then it may actually make those price gains happen. Even a few analysts on its side might make all the difference.

Is Boeing a Good Stock to Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on BA stock based on 19 Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average BA price target of $234.78 per share implies 42.7% upside potential.

data.title: Trump Demands Investigation After U.S. GDP Growth Is Revised to 4.3%
data.description:
President Donald Trump demanded an investigation on Thursday after the U.S. government revised third-quarter economic growth to 4.3% from 3.4%. The 0.9-percentage-point increase followed an initial report released on October 29, just five days before the November 3 midterm elections. Trump accused government officials of deliberately publishing a lower figure to influence the election, although he offered no evidence to support that claim.

In a Truth Social post on Thanksgiving, Trump called the original figures "FAKE" and the revision a "massive, and purposeful, error."

The figures came from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), which measures the value of goods and services produced in the U.S. Its first estimate showed that the economy had grown at an annualized rate of 3.4% between July and September.

An annualized GDP rate shows how fast the economy would grow over a full year if the same quarterly pace continued. It does not mean output increased by 4.3% in just three months. The BEA also adjusts for inflation, so higher prices alone do not count as real economic growth.

That was already stronger than the 2.2% growth recorded in the second quarter. However, the November 25 update showed that economic activity was actually stronger than initially estimated.

Why the Government Revised Its GDP Figures

The BEA typically releases several estimates of quarterly economic growth because some information is unavailable when it prepares its first report. Interestingly, the agency said the new figures showed that changes to software price data accounted for much of that adjustment.

Consumer spending was also revised higher, partly because updated retail figures showed stronger purchases of goods such as pharmaceuticals and computer accessories.

A study coauthored by the BEA's director found that GDP estimates released roughly 90 days after initial estimates differed by an average of about 0.52 percentage points over the past 25 years.

Unsurprisingly, Trump has challenged government economic figures before. In August 2025, he fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a weak jobs report, without providing evidence that the figures had been manipulated.

The BEA has scheduled its next estimate of third-quarter GDP for December 23, when another round of economic data will be included.

data.title: Salesforce (CRM) Price Forecast: What Financial Analysts Expect Ahead of Q3 Earnings Next Week
data.description:
Salesforce (CRM) is set to report Q3 earnings next week on December 2. The company's share price is down around 25% so far this year, mainly because of investors worrying about how it can compete against the growth of AI alternatives such as agents and assistants. It does have its own AI Agentforce tools it is looking to develop, but investors remain skeptical about how quickly these can generate revenues.

Wall Street analysts expect CRM to report earnings per share of $3.45, an improvement on the $3.25 it reported in the same period last year. Its revenues are tipped to come in at $11.46 billion, up on the $10.3 billion the company reported this time last year. Heading into earnings, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus on the stock.

Latest Analysts' Views on CRM Stock

Four-star analyst Tal Liani of Bank of America Securities recently maintained a Buy rating on Salesforce, retaining the price target of $285.00. Liani believes that Salesforce can resume stronger organic growth in the second half of fiscal 2027, supported by improving current remaining performance obligations and a solid pipeline. The recent share-price decline also creates a more favorable near-term risk-reward profile, Liani said, while the company's broad portfolio addresses major enterprise AI needs across data, applications, automation, and user interaction.
Partner feedback points to additional upside from cross-selling, regional expansion, and continued Data Cloud activity within Salesforce's existing customer base. Although Agentforce monetization is developing gradually as clients evaluate costs and prepare their data, Liani believes adoption can expand over time.

However, Tyler Radke, analyst at Citi, reiterated a Hold rating on Salesforce, with a price target of $198.00 down from $263. He pointed to uneven demand for Salesforce's core products and customers' continued caution about larger, longer-term commitments. He expects only a modest third-quarter performance improvement. He added that AI offerings such as Agentforce and Data Cloud are growing, but adoption is still limited.

Danni Hewson, AJ Bell head of financial analysis, said: "Salesforce shares continue to languish on investor scepticism over whether the company can successfully reposition from a traditional provider of customer relationship management services into a fully automated AI platform." She said that a key metric to watch out for is remaining performance obligations. Any slowing from the prior quarter's 14% growth rate will be seen as disappointing.

"Salesforce needs to demonstrate that Agentforce is generating incremental spending rather than simply replacing existing software licences," she said.

Is CRM a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On TipRanks, CRM has a Strong Buy consensus based on 30 Buy and 9 Hold ratings. Its highest price target is $400. CRM stock's consensus price target is $276.88, implying a 40.40% upside. (See CRM Stock Forecast.)
